priceSnapshot.note: Up 0.16 percent on the rolling 24h open of 79,480.1, and DOWN 94.7 points - 0.12 percent - against the 79,704.6 midnight mark. The flat headline hides a real round trip: from the midnight snapshot price slid five straight hourly bars into a 79,001.0 low on the 10:00Z bar, a 703.6-point drawdown worth 1.52 hourly ATRs, then reclaimed 608.9 of it in ninety minutes. The 24h high of 81,499.9 is the all-time print this desk recorded on the 01:00Z bar and is now 1,890.0 points overhead.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $79,400.0 AND a failure to reclaim it on either of the next two hourly bars. Spot is 209.9 points above it, 0.45 hourly ATRs at the current 463.06 - inside the 0.4-to-0.6 ATR band every gate in this log has been written in. The level is structural, not round: it sits 87.4 points under the 1H EMA50 at 79,487.35 that price reclaimed on the 10:00Z bar, so a settled close below 79,400.0 means the reclaim failed rather than merely wobbled. Midday 27 August's proposal to widen the reclaim window from two bars to four when hourly ATR is CONTRACTING again does not apply: ATR has fallen only from 488.22 to 463.06, a 5.2 percent contraction, but the amendment was written for a contracting-into-quiet tape and this morning produced a 841.8-point range, so the standard two-bar clause is kept.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $79,880.0. Spot is 270.1 points below it, 0.58 hourly ATRs - inside the band. The level clears three things at once: the 1H EMA20 at 79,758.65 that price has been beneath since the 02:00Z bar, the 79,750.0 liquidation shelf where 1,430,012 USD of two-sided fills sit, and the 79,842.8 morning high. A close above it re-opens the 80,000.0 magnet.

decisionBox.changed: Midnight held an 85 percent spot core, flat futures and 84.91 USDT of idle cash after taking profit into the failed breakout. This session re-deploys 22 USDT of that cash into the spot core - the position flips from TAKE_PROFIT to ADD. The gates move down with price: the reduce level comes from 79,480.0 to 79,400.0 and the add level from 80,050.0 to 79,880.0, both re-anchored to the current 463.06 ATR.

liquidation.note: 1,430,012 USD across 165 fills, split almost evenly at 48.2 percent short-side. It is the nearest cluster above spot at 140.1 points, 0.30 hourly ATRs, and the even split is what makes it interesting: both books got hurt here, so it is a genuine battleground rather than a one-sided flush.

1,726,461 USD across 134 fills and only 0.9 percent short-side, so essentially the whole bucket is LONGS being taken out. It is the single heaviest cluster in the 20.8h window and sits 390.1 points above spot, 0.84 hourly ATRs. Marked as the magnet because it is the largest mapped cluster and because it doubles as the round-number shelf. Same caveat as every session: this records where forced flow ALREADY happened on the way down through the level, not resting orders sitting there now.

1,446,461 USD across 144 fills, 85.4 percent short-side. From here up the character of the map inverts - 80,500.0, 80,750.0, 81,000.0 and 81,250.0 are 85 to 100 percent SHORT liquidations, the fuel that carried the overnight squeeze to 81,499.9.
1,360,464 USD across 172 fills, 99.1 percent short-side. The deepest short-side pocket of the window and the reason a reclaim of 80,000.0 would not be a quiet move.
818,935 USD across 193 fills, 90.5 percent long-side. The first shelf under spot at 109.9 points and the shallowest of the three below - it was chewed through this morning without a pause.

1,198,061 USD across 196 fills and ZERO percent short-side - a pure long-liquidation flush. This is where the 09:00Z and 10:00Z bars did their damage and it is the level that has to hold on any retest.

374,123 USD across 93 fills, also 100 percent long-side. Thin by USD, which cuts both ways: the 79,001.0 low stopped one point above it, so the shelf was tested and held, but there is not much forced flow left below to absorb a second visit.

calibration.rollingRecord: Sixteen sessions logged. Add gates fired and were collected on three consecutive sessions (27 August midnight and morning, 26 August midday); midday 27 August produced the window's first whipsawed gate; endday 27 August's reduce gate fired and confirmed cleanly with its stop hit; midnight 28 August's reduce gate has now produced the window's SECOND whipsaw. Two whipsaws in four sessions with gates placed inside the same 0.4-to-0.6 ATR band is the first sign that band may be too tight for the current tape.
calibration.note: Midnight's REDUCE gate at a settled 1H close below 79,480.0 FIRED at the 09:00Z close of 79,283.4 - 196.6 points through the line - but it did NOT CONFIRM. The rule requires a failure to reclaim on either of the next two hourly bars, and the very next bar, 10:00Z, closed 79,573.6, a clean 93.6 points back above. Acting on the raw trigger would have sold at or near 79,283.4 against a current 79,609.9, so acting_helped is FALSE by 326.5 points. Midnight's ADD gate at 80,050.0 did NOT fire: the highest settled close since the snapshot was 79,666.0 on the 07:00Z bar, 384.0 points short. The gate was placed 243.9 points out at 0.51 hourly ATRs, correctly inside the band - which is precisely why the second whipsaw in four sessions is worth logging rather than dismissing. PROPOSAL FOR MIDDAY: on any session where the PRIOR gate whipsawed, widen the reclaim window from two bars to three before recording a confirmation. That is a smaller change than midday 27 August's ATR-conditional four-bar proposal, which is still untested, and it targets the actual failure mode observed twice now.
